It is critical to the United States’ ability to utilize financial information to combat terrorism, terrorist financing, money laundering, and other financial crimes.

supported_results.question: When is a Currency Transaction Report required for large cash transactions?
supported_results.answer: A bank must file a Currency Transaction Report (CTR) (FinCEN Form 104) for each transaction in currency76 (deposit, withdrawal, exchange, or other payment or transfer) of more than $10,000 by, through, or to the bank. Certain types of currency transactions need not be reported, such as those involving “exempt persons,” a group which can include retail or commercial customers meeting specific criteria for exemption. Refer to the core overview section, “Currency Transaction Reporting Exemptions,” pages 90 to 94, for further guidance.

supported_results.question: How should transaction testing samples be selected during a CIP examination?
supported_results.answer: On the basis of a risk assessment, prior examination reports, and a review of the bank’s audit findings, select a sample of new accounts opened since the most recent examination. The sample should include a cross-section of accounts (e.g., consumers and businesses, loans and deposits, credit card relationships, and Internet accounts).

supported_results.question: What is structuring and why is it prohibited?
supported_results.answer: The definition of structuring, as set forth in 31 CFR 103.11(gg) (which was implemented before a USA PATRIOT Act provision extended the prohibition on structuring to geographic targeting orders and BSA recordkeeping requirements), states, “a person structures a transaction if that person, acting alone, or in conjunction with, or on behalf of, other persons, conducts or attempts to conduct one or more transactions in currency in any amount, at one or less than $10,000. The transactions need not exceed the $10,000 CTR filing threshold at any one bank on any single day in order to constitute structuring. Money launderers and criminals have developed many ways to structure large amounts of currency to evade the CTR or a geographic targeting order reporting requirement.

supported_results.question: How long must required BSA records be retained?
supported_results.answer: A bank must retain the identifying information about a customer for a period of five years after the date the account is closed.
